variants.headline: A new government takes shape
variants.sub: The colony has a newly formed government.
variants.body:
A new government has been formed in {colony}. Its formation establishes an administration; it does not establish the success of its future decisions. In considering {target}, the useful distinction is between assembling a government and meeting the obligations that come with governing.

We welcome the contribution of {target}. Forming an administration is a legitimate achievement, and it deserves recognition without requiring us to pretend that every future difficulty has already been solved.

variants.headline: Formation is the beginning of governing
variants.sub: Government formation has produced a new administration in {colony}.
variants.body:
Government formation is a beginning. The new administration in {colony} gives public attention an institutional focus, while leaving its practical record to be made. Any judgment of {target} should recognise both the significance of formation and the limits of what formation alone can demonstrate.

We welcome the contribution of {target}. Forming an administration is a legitimate achievement, and it deserves recognition without requiring us to pretend that every future difficulty has already been solved.

variants.headline: New ministry, practical obligations
variants.sub: A new government has been formed in {colony}.
variants.body:
The colony has a new government. There is an obvious temptation to read a whole political future into that fact. A more useful approach to {target} begins with the administration that has actually been formed and the responsibilities inherent in exercising public authority.

We welcome the contribution of {target}. Forming an administration is a legitimate achievement, and it deserves recognition without requiring us to pretend that every future difficulty has already been solved.
